sources.entry: Gesher - Open-source MCP servers and CLIs that let AI assistants read and edit Apple Notes, Reminders, Calendar, Contacts, Maps, Weather and Freeform. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/EphraimElgrabli/gesher) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.one_liner: Gesher is a set of native Swift MCP servers and command-line tools that let AI assistants such as Claude, Codex or Cursor read and edit Apple Notes, Reminders, Calendar, Contacts, Maps, Weather and Freeform on a Mac.
use_cases: let an AI assistant add and organize Reminders
edit Apple Notes with Markdown, checklists and tables from an agent
read agenda and find free time in Calendar
draw or annotate Freeform boards from an AI chat
look up contacts or check weather and routes while planning
how_to_run: Download gesher-<app>-1.2.0.mcpb from the latest release and open it in Claude Desktop (one bundle per app)
Or paste the install prompt into Claude Code, Codex or Cursor
Or run: curl -fsSL <installer URL> | bash (installs all seven apps into ~/.local)
Run `gesher permissions` in a new Terminal window and click Allow
Grant Full Disk Access for Notes and Freeform when Gesher opens that window
stack: Apple EventKit and other Apple frameworks
notable: 134 tools across seven apps, with Reminders sections, smart lists, Notes tags and tables, and editable Freeform diagrams
Works without opening the apps; Freeform opens in the background only for imports
Every write is read back to verify, and bulk deletes are backed up first
Installer needs no sudo, checks the download's SHA-256, and backs up AI app config files before editing
Each app is also a command-line tool, e.g. calendar-cli agenda tomorrow
caveats: Requires an Apple silicon Mac running macOS 26 or later; tested on macOS 27
Uses private Apple frameworks, so a macOS update can break parts of it; labelled experimental
Maps is read-only; minute-by-minute rain forecasts are available only in some countries
